name: 5G Core Network Upgrade — Phase 2
description: Phase 2 of the nationwide 5G core rollout targeting Tier-2 cities in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Planned to expand capacity by 40% and reduce backhaul latency to sub-10ms for enterprise SLA customers.
outcome_summary: Project placed on hold after the NSA architecture decision was identified as technically unsound. Root cause traced to DEC decision. Three of five milestones delayed. Awaiting architecture review board decision before resuming.

lessons_learned.description: Vendor evaluation criteria must include a 3-year total-cost-of-ownership model and an explicit NSA-to-SA migration path before any procurement decision is ratified at the Architecture Review Board. Cross-functional review from Network Operations and Finance is mandatory for all decisions exceeding ₹2 crore CapEx.

name: Optical Transport Layer Expansion — Bengaluru-Mumbai Corridor
description: Strategic capacity expansion of the Bengaluru-Mumbai optical transport corridor from 200G to 800G to support 5G backhaul, enterprise MPLS growth, and IoT platform traffic. Project was initially on-hold following a capacity breach incident. Corrective actions unblocked the project which subsequently completed ahead of revised schedule.
outcome_summary: Project successfully completed on 15 September, 3.5 months ahead of the revised planned end date. The Bengaluru-Mumbai optical segment now operates at 800G with 45% headroom at current traffic levels. Enterprise MPLS SLA compliance improved to 99.98% post-completion. The corrective action for emergency capacity upgrade was the key enabler for project recovery.

lessons_learned.description: Capacity models for new platform deployments must include a sensitivity analysis for 3x traffic growth scenarios. The IoT platform capacity model used at project approval underestimated traffic growth by 340%, directly causing the P2 incident and a 3-month project delay. All future platform projects must obtain a NOC capacity sign-off before go-live approval is granted.
